# Game profile of Ace Attorney Investigations Collection (Switch, base game v0 + update 1.0.0.2 = v131072). Plays on the Mac and on the iPhone
# Format: see dm/games/README.md
# Unity 2022.3.17f1 (IL2CPP), SDK 17.5.3: the shaders are Shader objects in the Addressables bundles and the player's serialized files (read by shader_split.py through unityfs.py).
# Unity 2022's Switch subprograms, the IL2CPP file API and the first boots were worked out by armyja (GitHub issues #17, #18, #19 and pull requests #15, #16)

# ---- Identity ----
title_id	010005501E68C000
program_id	010005501E68C000

# ---- App ----
# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
name	Ace Attorney Investigations Collection
ipa	AceAttorneyInvestigations.ipa
app_category	public.app-category.adventure-games

# ---- Versions ----
# only the merged 1.0.0.2 copy is extracted
build	v131072	1.0.0.2	main=f2755f077e2b2dfd89e1c59dcddce91e	subsdk0=2f9e7f4ec017bb00e214af7c2fd70f4b	sdk=311deab1f062b504f3d646a49ddcd4e8
package	v131072
shader_versions	v131072

# ---- Files ----
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie)
modules	main subsdk0 sdk
romfs_marker	Data/globalgamemanagers
zip_store	.assets:.bundle:.dat:.json:.resource:.ress:.metallib

# ---- Memory ----
# The NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource, so IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is true: nninitStartup (main+0x874b00) hands application pool − used memory to StandardAllocator as virtual address memory,
# one 1 GB-aligned address region in the alias region, and never calls SetMemoryHeapSize. SDK 17's AddressRegionManager takes about 1 GB of the alias region as its node area first;
# dm/tools/sdk_patches.py registers a cut for this sdk build that shrinks it to 62 MB, as for Fire Emblem Engage. Unity's own allocator (main+0x40f1d4 → AllocateAddressRegion) reserves its pools beside it,
# each aligned by its size. Measured over the first five minutes (title, Episode 1's opening, the first investigation; probes on VammManager::AllocateAddressRegion's success path sdk+0x1395a8
# and FreeAddressRegion sdk+0x139df0, commits from the MapPhysicalMemory log): with Engage's 2.5 GB pool StandardAllocator reserved 2.44 GB and committed only 0.19 GB, Unity's pools held 1.06 GB,
# and after 140 s the live regions ended 4.37 GB into the 4.375 GB alias region. Over ten minutes of the same route, a 1.5 GB pool (StandardAllocator 1.44 GB at +0.75 GB) let them reach +3.91 GB,
# a 1 GB pool +2.85 GB. So the pool is reported as 1 GB: StandardAllocator gets 0.94 GB (five times its use) right after the node area, and running out of address space is a crash, while
# a pool a little smaller than what the game maps in all (1.02 GB at the peak) changes nothing: the host does not enforce it and only nninitStartup reads it
# The block is Engage's 5 GB: 256 MB in front + 4.375 GB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 128 MB heap region (the game never calls SetHeapSize)
mem_reserve	0x140000000
mem_alias	0x118000000
mem_stack	0x10000000
app_pool	0x40000000

# ---- Shader split (shader_split.py; Unity Shader objects, read by unityfs.py) ----
# engine built-ins (the unitybuiltinshaders bundle, Resources/) go to engine, the player's serialized files to data, the other Addressables bundles to assets
shader_groups	_unitybuiltinshaders_=engine /Resources/=engine /StreamingAssets/=assets /Data/=data
shader_note	Ace Attorney Investigations Collection shaders
notes: Update 1.0.0.2 (v131072) over the base game, which is an XCI; its DLC NSP is a licence only. SDK 17.5.3. Unity 2022.3.17f1 IL2CPP on NVN. Modules `main`, `subsdk0` (the movie module, `NintendoSDK_movie`) and `sdk`. Plays on the iPhone; 60 fps, as on the Switch (present interval 1). On the Mac it was brought up through the first-boot settings, the title, Investigations 1's menus and Episode 1's opening and first investigation up to the first Logic prompt (25 minutes with no red line). Much of the bring-up was worked out first by armyja in a fork (GitHub issues #17, #18, #19 and pull requests #15, #16). | Setting | Where | Why | |---|---|---| | Node area cut 1 GB → 62 MB; regions of 4 MB and more aligned to 2 MB | the SDK-wide rules in `dm/tools/sdk_patches.py` (the AddressRegionManager constructor at `sdk+0x139458`: the movs at `+0x139468` and `+0x1394fc`; the placement's alignments at `+0x139654`, `+0x13965c`, `+0x139660`) | without it `StandardAllocator::Initialize(nullptr, pool − use

mem_used	0x4800000

# ---- Textures ----
# Movie frames (VP9, NV12 to a buffer): the game copies each frame into a 1280x720 R8 and a 640x360 RG8 texture in a CPU-visible pool and publishes them with
# nvnMemoryPoolFlushMappedRange; without the upload the intro movie stayed black under its "+ Skip" prompt
tex_flush_upload	on

# ---- Presentation ----
# The Switch version shows 30 fps and steps the game a fixed amount per update: a KIDS task waits out 1/30 s and steps the game clock by 1/30 s, the battle steps 1 / the game's frame-rate
# block (30.0), and the event scripts step by the KTGL device's frame rate (59.94 / present interval 2). On 1.3.0 main (patches.py FRAME_STEP) three stubs run the updates at the cap
# and set all three to it (with only a 1/60 s wait the clock and the battles ran at twice real time); the host paces the presents at 60 fps, 30 when 60 does not hold.
# 0 = the Switch original
fps_target	60
# The updates step by the cap whatever the hold, so holding late frames only paces the screen: frames are shown as soon as they are ready (the 60fps IPA ran battles at 45–57).
# The iPhone battle's GPU going from 10 to 41 ms a frame was first read as its GPU clock following the hold; the same rise came with no hold at all: the battle runs about 1,000 to
# 2,800 compute dispatches a frame after its first cutscene, which each had an encoder of their own (nvn_mtl.m dispatch_enc)
fps_hold	off
# KTGL binds whole mesh pools (up to ~590,000 vertices) and its soldiers' Half2 / Short2 attributes feed integer shader inputs, which the replay converts on the CPU:
# over the bound ranges that was millions of vertices a frame in battle (26 fps at any target on the Mac); only over the vertices each draw reads. Shadow vertex inputs
# (nvn_mtl.m vin_on) now take those attributes on the GPU; this still serves the draws that keep the CPU conversion (transform feedback, DM_NVN_VCONV_CPU=1)
vconv_range	on

# ---- Files ----
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie, which main imports from; the sdk is STEINS;GATE RE:BOOT's build)
modules	main subsdk0 sdk
romfs_marker	FFRS/Content/Paks/FFRS-Switch.ucas
zip_store	.pak:.ttf:.txt:.ucas:.utoc:.metallib

# ---- Graphics ----
# 60 fps (30 on the Switch): the engine's Switch device profile sets rhi.syncinterval=2 (BaseSwitchDeviceProfiles.ini), so the game asks for present interval 2, and the game sets no t.MaxFPS.
# The host writes rhi.SyncInterval 1 into its console variable (hle_fpslock.c), whenever the game sets it back (at level loads), so the game asks for present interval 1 itself. Unreal steps
# the game by the time that really passed: DM_NVN_REGLUM traces of the same keys from the same save at 30 and 60 fps (59.8 fps, frame time p99 18 ms on the Mac) match from the load
# through a 3 s walk (thumbnail difference ≤ 0.006). DM_FPS_TARGET=30 (Documents/env.txt on the iPhone) keeps the game's 30 and saves power
fps_target	60

# ---- Memory ----
# Unreal Engine 5.6.1: nninitStartup (main+0x13370) reserves one 62 GB region for the engine, and its FMallocBinned3
# (38 GB of address space) is constructed in place in the bss; the constructor call is cut and the host runs Unreal's heap on a malloc zone (dm/tools/ue_malloc.py, hle_uemalloc.c layout UE5_6),
# and the SDK's node area is cut to 62 MB. The engine hands the region out with a page allocator of its own (main+0x13ef0): a bump pointer, and freed blocks kept in free lists by size
# class, so its address use only grows, and past the region's end OnOutOfMemory (main+0x13c74) aborts. Probed at main+0x13fcc from the save in the first field, through the first battle:
# a 1 GB block at boot (a static constructor), the high-water mark at +1.50 GB 15 s in, +1.77 GB at 56 s, +2.02 GB at 166 s; a 2 GB region (DRAGON QUEST VII Reimagined's) aborted in that
# battle. This SDK build aligns regions of 2 MB and more to 2 MB only (VammManager::AllocateAddressRegion, sdk+0x145e00), so the region starts right after the node area, and
# the rewriter's engine-wide gate on the store of its size (dm/tools/ue_region.py; hle_svc.c) gives it what the alias region has room for in Engage's 5 GB block (256 MB in front + 4.375 GB alias region
# + 256 MB stack region + 128 MB heap region): 4.06 GB (until 2026-10-31 -SwitchVirtualAddressSpaceSize=4064 in game_args). On the Mac in the field and the first battle, with 4064 MB:
# about 1 GB of the alias region mapped, an Unreal heap of 1 GB, 2.2-2.4 GB resident and 1.2-1.5 GB of Metal allocations
mem_reserve	0x140000000
mem_alias	0x118000000
mem_stack	0x10000000
app_pool	0xCD500000
# the NPDM declares 20 MB of system resource
sys_resource	0x1400000

# ---- Input ----
# A 3D field whose camera the right stick tilts and turns: the 3D pad layout. It plays docked (1920x1080)
pad_layout	full

# ---- NVN ----
# 2,077 vertex shaders (Unreal's particle vertex factories) pick one of several c2 table slots at run time: texture table words 0x168-0x1c0 and sampler table words 0x568-0x590, and no other
# word of c2. The translator cannot trace them to one slot: slot indices in c2, the bound slots in its arrays (without the key the first one aborted the host in a double free, now fixed)
tex_dyn_slots	on

# ---- Shader split ----
# The two shader libraries of the IoStore container FFRS-Switch.utoc / .ucas (no shader code archive in the pak): the engine's global shaders and the game's material shaders. Their tables and
# shader groups are Oodle-compressed, which the game's own decoder undoes in the Mac host's tool mode (uepak.py Toc / io_archive / OodleHost, no boot). Unreal combines vertex and pixel
# shaders per draw from its pipeline state, so every vertex shader is made to link with any pixel shader (shader_split.py separable_pairs)
shader_groups	ShaderArchive-Global-=global ShaderArchive-=game
shader_note	FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE shaders

# ---- Presentation ----
# The original sets present interval 2 (30 fps on the Switch) through QualitySettings.vSyncCount. Frame-counted logic steps by GameTime.VsyncFixedCount (= vSyncCount, read back through
# the getter), so a count of 1 at 60 fps runs at the speed of the original at 30 fps. The rewriter finds the current quality level's count through Unity's internal-call table
# (dm/tools/unity_fps.py) and the host writes 60 / fps_target into it (hle_fpslock.c), with the present cap at the same rate; until 2026-11-09 a cut on 2.0.0 main held the setter's argument at 1.
# Measured on the Mac (holding Down for 0.45 s in the save list): 60 fps with a count of 1 and the original 30 fps both move 6 slots; 60 fps with a count of 2 (DM_PRESENT_INTERVAL=display) reaches the end (9 or more)
fps_target	60

# ---- Memory ----
# The NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource, so IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is true: nninitStartup hands all free memory (application pool − 64 MB) to StandardAllocator as virtual address memory,
# one address region in the alias region (1 GB aligned). Unity's low-level virtual allocator also calls AllocateAddressRegion itself (each block aligned by size: 2.25 MB takes 4 MB, 16.25 MB takes 20 MB),
# about 1.05 GB in the prologue battle. Newer SDKs' AddressRegionManager first takes about 1 GB at the start of the alias region as its node area; dm/tools/sdk_patches.py registers a cut for this game's sdk build that shrinks it to 62 MB (the hardware's alias region is 64 GB and does not care).
# Measured (prologue to the battle, 12 minutes): StandardAllocator commits only 0.58 GB and Unity's own regions 0.97 GB, 1.55 GB in all. So the pool is reported as 2.5 GB (StandardAllocator about 2.44 GB, four times its use),
# and the block fits in 5 GB = 256 MB in front + 4.375 GB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 128 MB heap region (Engage never calls SetHeapSize; thread stacks are placed at random in the stack region). 5 GB is the total proven on a phone (D2R);
# without the "extended virtual addressing" entitlement iOS allows one reservation of at most 6 GB, but Metal and the rest need address space too (Engage allocates about 1 GB of GPU memory on the Mac), so the former 6 GB block left no margin on a phone.
mem_reserve	0x140000000
mem_alias	0x118000000
mem_stack	0x10000000
app_pool	0xA0000000

# engine built-ins (data.unity3d, Resources/unity default resources) go to engine, the Addressables bundles to assets
shader_groups	/data.unity3d=engine /Resources/=engine /StreamingAssets/=assets
shader_note	Fire Emblem Engage shaders
# the NVN depth mode the game sets (nvnDeviceSetDepthMode near = 0): the pipeline archive made offline holds the main0_z vertex entries (dm/gfx/tools/pso_offline.py)
depth_mode	zero

# ---- Files ----
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk2 = NintendoSDK_movie, for FNA3D's video player). Not loaded: subsdk0 (NVIDIA's Vulkan driver) and subsdk1 (NVIDIA's OpenGL driver):
# main imports EGL and Vulkan for SDL3's GL / Vulkan support, but FNA3D renders with NVN, and both drivers program the GPU through NvRm, which the host does not have
modules	main subsdk2 sdk

# ---- Memory ----
# The NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource (virtual address memory), and main never calls SetMemoryHeapSize: everything lives in address regions of the alias region.
# Measured with a 64 GB alias region from boot into the first level (probes on VammManager::AllocateAddressRegion's success path sdk+0x13bf8c, x21 size / x22 address, and the MapPhysicalMemory log):
#   - malloc's StandardAllocator, 40 GB of address space (main+0x28c084; 1.1.1 main+0x28bff4); 2.19 GB used, 1.75 GB of it FNA3D's GPU heap (FNA3D_CreateDevice). stdalloc_cap below gives it 2.5 GB;
#   - the .NET GC's region range: 5 × its hard limit, 768 MB (75% of the 1 GB its GetPhysicalMemoryLimit, main+0x28c08c; 1.1.1 main+0x28bffc, returns), i.e. 3.75 GB. game_env below sets 1.5 GB, which the GC
#     uses from both ends (756 MB from the start, 748 MB from the end, 718 MB mapped into the first level);

mem_alias	0x118000000
mem_stack	0x10000000

game_env	DOTNET_GCRegionRange=60000000

stdalloc_cap	0xa0000000
